content.content:
### Commons and archive

Generation zero of the archive seeds every island with more than one root so the novelty term has variance to weight; an `inconclusive` experiment verdict maps to a `parked` variant status with a configured retest cap before the variant is marked `dominated`; `ParentSample` carries sibling summaries so the quarantined Harness Engineer does not re-explore known dead ends; `LeaderboardRow` gains `harnessVariantId`; `deprecated` skills stay re-samplable when a later diagnosis names a context they were never tested in, closing only on a human rejection; and the manifest writer flags the same `KnowledgeProposal` digest appearing independently in two departments as the trigger for a portfolio-level nomination, which is how a norm like the Village's unprompted "receipt culture" would reach promotion on evidence rather than by acclamation.

### Governance

Five transitions never complete without a `signoff/recorded` event naming the principal and the artefact hash: spec freeze, relaxation of a security or compliance check, review acceptance, release, and training-data release; every client-district session carries `dataUse/terms` from creation; the exporter refuses to run without a redaction profile; publishing a raw excerpt is a signed decision; the EU AI Act's serious-incident channel is separate from the failure blog and routed to counsel; no training run that could approach the systemic-risk compute threshold starts before `ModelLineage` and its threshold alarm exist; and no named comparison of a competitor's model appears before the paired-experiment discipline and the isolation proof that make it verifiable.

## Council review

Six judges reviewed the first draft with the AI Village sources and the harness source in hand; their full reports are kept with the session's research files. Scores are out of ten.

| Judge | Lens | Score | Decisive finding, and what changed |
|---|---|---|---|
| J1 | Software factory and client | 3 | No compliance artefact on a four-month sales clock; cost per certified session has no producer; the outreach ban was a promise. Shift zero became NDA-gated and Proving Ground only; `district` on the stamp; the composition gate; the trust dossier as the client-facing export. |
| J2 | Open-endedness and archives | 7 | Archive mechanics faithful to the source algorithms, but `inconclusive` had no status, generation zero had one root, and no path took emergent value to promotion. The Commons and archive section. |
| J3 | Reinforcement-learning data | 6 | Always-on is a scheduling wrapper around W3's mechanism; `policyVersion` and `seed` are missing from the stamp; truncated rollouts score as failures; the dataset's licence forbids training. The Data section. |
| J5 | Determinism and verification | 4 | The certificate does not carry its executor and an agent-reported run certifies identically; hidden checks are false for a shell-capable implementer until slice 5; tamper is the cheapest missing gate. Executor moved into slice 4 and the publication rules. |
| J6 | Governance and EU compliance | 3 | The draft claimed slices 1–4 and quarantine as landed; approvals carry no principal; export has no consent or redaction gate; comparative-advertising exposure. The Governance section and the status column. |
| J8 | Operations | 3 | Nothing above one session resumes after a crash; no shift-level budget, no circuit breaker, no retention, no durable scheduler; a cost model with stated assumptions. Shift zero's runbook and the Budgets section. |

## Alternatives considered

**Copy the Village format.** Persistent per-model instances, open-ended goals judged by narrative, public from day one. Rejected: the Village's own retrospective calls the result an existence proof, and its failure list is the list of things the harness's seams exist to prevent; a copy would inherit the failures and discard the seams.

**Publish named frontier comparisons from day one.** Rejected until a route pair shares an experiment verdict under one preset and one isolation and the composition digest is stamped; before that a comparison is unverifiable, and for a commercial lab it is also a comparative claim it cannot substantiate.

**An offline batch pipeline instead of an always-on one.** Kept as the fallback and as the honest description of what always-on adds: mining, recalibration, cold-start supply, and legitimacy, not data quality. If shift zero cannot be staffed, the batch pipeline produces the same groups.

**One weekly cadence for every district.** Rejected for the Workshop, where a calendar reset would put a human signer under a deadline unrelated to the artefact and would force restarts on a layer that cannot yet resume.

**Nonprofit-style disclosure of raw transcripts.** Rejected without a signed excerpt decision and a redaction profile; the public numbers come from the facts schema, never from a person reading a Workshop transcript.

## Acceptance criteria

- Shift zero runs the Proving Ground for seven days with every cell present as a row (report or error) and no missing sequence in the persisted logs, with a human on call and every intervention logged with a principal.
- The observatory shows `isolation`, executor, composition digest (or `pending`), and tamper status on every row, publishes no ranking without an `ExperimentResult` verdict, and names no frontier route before the composition digest is stamped; a snapshot test proves the withholding of Workshop and held-out sessions from the public export.
- `verify-village-composition` exists beside `verify-cordis-config`, in `hygiene` and the static CI lanes, over the same configuration inventory: a district composition — one composing `@deepseek-ai/dsh-environment-runner`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-fleet`, or `@deepseek-ai/dsh-experiments` — is rejected when it omits `@deepseek-ai/dsh-budget-policy` with at least one cap set, a session persistence backend, or `@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-checkpoint-policy`, and a fleet entry is rejected when it omits `workspaceRetention`; a runner claiming `isolation: process` or `host` warns until `--strict`, because no read-barrier slice on this branch proves the claim. Every rejection is proven by a fixture, and each names the file, the entry id, and the rule. Still needed: refusal of an outreach-capable tool composed without the monitor, which waits for the `external-communication` authority.
- A certificate carries its executor; an agent-reported run cannot certify above `none`; a tamper fixture yields reward zero before any public certificate rate is published.
- Cost per certified session appears only once a `usage/priced` event with the pricing-table digest exists and the scorekeeper folds it; a fixture proves the same log prices identically after the table changes when the digest differs.
- A session derived from the AI Village dataset carries data-use terms scoped to evaluation and never appears in a training export, proven by an export fixture.

## Rollout

1. **Shift zero (Proving Ground, NDA).** Landed: `district` on the `environment/run` stamp with the exporter's `withheldDistricts` and per-request `districts`, the fleet's per-route circuit breaker (`FLEET_ROUTE_BREAKER_OPEN`), its plan-level `tokenCeiling` with the run's `spend` (`FLEET_TOKEN_CEILING_REACHED`), its `workspaceRetention`, the composition gate, the budget policy's `usage/priced` event carrying the pricing-table digest, the executor on certificates (read-barrier slice 4), the scorekeeper's fold of `usage/priced` into a cost per session and a cost per certified session, and the stamp's `district` as part of the `ScoreboardRow` key the observatory withholds by. Still needed: runs with a human on call.
2. **Public certificate rates.** Needs read-barrier slices 5 and 6 (shell denial and tamper verdicts) and the tamper column; rates then feed the archive's quality term.
3. **Unattended shifts.** Designed in the [shifts note](2026-09-05-village-shifts.md): shift identity and the `shift/*` ledger, cells recovered from their stamps and never run twice, cadence per district, and the token spend window across shifts; the host-level supervisor becomes a fallback once its slices land.
4. **Named comparisons and the Commons.** Needs the composition manifest slices (digest on the stamp, preset as an experiment arm, `harnessVariantId` on the leaderboard) and the archive with `parked` and sibling summaries.
5. **Workshop in public and excerpt disclosure.** Needs `signoff/recorded`, `dataUse/terms`, mandatory redaction, and the trust-dossier export.
6. **Any outreach.** Needs the `external-communication` authority and the deny-capable monitor.
7. **A live observatory.** Needs the leaderboard as a cached session projection; until then the page states its batch refresh interval.
8. **Feeding W3.** Needs `policyVersion` and `seed` on the stamp, masked terminal reasons in the trajectory fold, near-duplicate admission, and the device-slot budget.

## Risks

- **A correct table under an overstated headline.** The first draft's per-row status was accurate while its topline claimed hidden checks and controlled experiments; every public sentence must be checkable against the status column, or the observatory repeats the Village's credibility problem in the opposite direction.
- **One missing row.** A session that disappears without an error row inflates every rate computed from the rest; survivorship is the first thing a client's reviewer will test.
- **Harness and model co-evolution.** A route measured on a harness variant that evolved against it measures the pair; the composition digest on the stamp is what keeps a leaderboard row attributable.
- **Comparative claims.** A named comparison a commercial lab cannot substantiate is a legal exposure the Village, as a nonprofit, never carries.
- **Sunk hardware.** Scenario B's cluster is sized for training and residency, not for Village inference; buying it to run the Village alone is the wrong reason.
- **Staffing dominates cost.** Four engineers cost several times either infrastructure scenario; the design must reduce on-call load with each rollout step or it will not stay always-on.
- **Emergent institutions.** Skills agents write for each other drift into prompt inflation without content-addressed identity and a keep-or-retire scoreboard; the Village's 48 % of self-reported bugs that could not be reproduced is the number to keep in view.

content.content:
### Commons 与归档

归档的第零代为每个岛播下不止一个根，让 novelty 项有方差可加权；`inconclusive` 的实验裁决映射到 `parked` 变体状态，并在标记为 `dominated` 之前有配置的重测上限；`ParentSample` 携带同胞摘要，使被隔离的 Harness Engineer 不再重新探索已知的死路；`LeaderboardRow` 新增 `harnessVariantId`；被标记 `deprecated` 的技能在后续诊断点名了一个它从未被测试过的语境时仍可被重新采样，只在人工拒绝时关闭；清单写入器把同一个 `KnowledgeProposal` 摘要在两个部门独立出现标记为组合级提名的触发条件，这就是像 Village 未经提示的"收据文化"这样的规范如何凭证据而非喝彩到达晋升。

### 治理

五个转换在没有指明主体与制品哈希的 `signoff/recorded` 事件之前绝不完成：规范冻结、放宽安全或合规检查、评审接受、发布，以及训练数据发布；每个客户区会话自创建起携带 `dataUse/terms`；导出器在没有脱敏配置时拒绝运行；发布原始摘录是一次签署的决定；欧盟 AI 法案的严重事件通道与失败博客分离并转交法务；任何可能接近系统性风险算力阈值的训练运行在 `ModelLineage` 及其阈值告警存在之前都不启动；在配对实验纪律与使之可验证的隔离证明到位之前，不出现任何对竞争对手模型的点名比较。

## Council review

六位评审带着 AI Village 的来源与 harness 源码评审了第一稿；他们的完整报告与本会话的研究文件保存在一起。分数满分为十。

| 评审 | 视角 | 分数 | 决定性发现，以及由此改变的内容 |
|---|---|---|---|
| J1 | 软件工厂与客户 | 3 | 四个月的销售周期上没有合规制品；每个已认证会话的成本没有生产者；外联禁令只是一个承诺。零号班次改为受 NDA 约束且仅限 Proving Ground；stamp 上的 `district`；组合门禁；作为面向客户导出的信任档案。 |
| J2 | 开放式演化与归档 | 7 | 归档机制忠实于源算法，但 `inconclusive` 没有状态、第零代只有一个根、没有路径把涌现的价值带到晋升。Commons 与归档一节。 |
| J3 | 强化学习数据 | 6 | 常驻运行是 W3 机制之上的调度包装；stamp 缺少 `policyVersion` 与 `seed`；被截断的 rollout 被记为失败；数据集许可证禁止训练。数据一节。 |
| J5 | 确定性与验证 | 4 | 证书不携带其 executor，agent 自报的运行同样能认证；在切片 5 之前对能用 shell 的实现者而言隐藏检查并不成立；篡改是最便宜的缺失门禁。executor 移入切片 4 与发布规则。 |
| J6 | 治理与欧盟合规 | 3 | 初稿声称切片 1–4 与隔离已落地；审批不携带主体；导出没有同意或脱敏门禁；比较广告的风险敞口。治理一节与状态列。 |
| J8 | 运营 | 3 | 单个会话之上没有任何东西能在崩溃后恢复；没有班次级预算、没有熔断器、没有保留策略、没有持久调度器；一个带明确假设的成本模型。零号班次的运行手册与预算一节。 |

## Alternatives considered

**照搬 Village 格式。** 每个模型一个持久实例、以叙事评判的开放式目标、从第一天起公开。已拒绝：Village 自己的回顾把结果称为存在性证明，而它的失败清单正是本 harness 各条 seam 意在防止的清单；照搬会继承失败而丢弃 seam。

**从第一天起发布点名的前沿模型比较。** 在一对路由共享同一 preset、同一隔离级别下的实验裁决且组合摘要已盖章之前均拒绝；在此之前比较无法验证，对一家商业实验室而言也是一项它无法证实的比较性声明。

**用离线批处理管线取代常驻运行。** 保留为后备方案，也是对常驻运行所增加内容的诚实描述：挖掘、重新校准、冷启动供给与正当性，而不是数据质量。如果零号班次无法配备人手，批处理管线产出同样的组。

**所有区统一每周节奏。** 对 Workshop 已拒绝，日历重置会让人工签署者面对与制品无关的截止期限，并在一个尚不能恢复的层上强制重启。

**非营利式地披露原始转录。** 在没有签署的摘录决定与脱敏配置之前已拒绝；公开数字来自事实 schema，绝不来自某人阅读 Workshop 转录。

## Acceptance criteria

- 零号班次运行 Proving Ground 七天，每个 cell 都以一行（报告或错误）出现，持久化日志中没有缺失的序号，有人值班且每次干预都连同主体一起记录。
- 观测台在每一行上显示 `isolation`、executor、组合摘要（或 `pending`）与篡改状态，没有 `ExperimentResult` 裁决就不发布排名，在组合摘要盖章之前不点名任何前沿路由；一个快照测试证明公开导出扣留了 Workshop 与留出会话。
- `verify-village-composition` 与 `verify-cordis-config` 并列存在，出现在 `hygiene` 与 CI 静态 lane 中，扫描同一份配置清单：区组合——即组合了 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-environment-runner`、`@deepseek-ai/dsh-fleet` 或 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-experiments` 的配置——如果缺少至少设置一个上限的 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-budget-policy`、缺少会话持久化后端或缺少 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-checkpoint-policy`，即被拒绝；fleet 条目缺少 `workspaceRetention` 也被拒绝；声明 `isolation: process` 或 `host` 的运行器只发出警告，直到使用 `--strict`，因为本分支上没有任何读取屏障切片能证明该声明。每条拒绝都由一个 fixture 证明，并且都会指明文件、条目 id 与规则。仍需要：拒绝在没有 monitor 的情况下组合能外联的工具，这要等 `external-communication` 权限。
- 证书携带其 executor；agent 自报的运行不能在 `none` 之上认证；在发布任何公开证书率之前，一个篡改 fixture 产出奖励零。
- 每个已认证会话的成本只在携带价格表摘要的 `usage/priced` 事件存在且 scorekeeper 折叠它之后出现；一个 fixture 证明价格表变更后同一份日志在摘要不同时定价不同。
- 由 AI Village 数据集派生的会话携带限定为评估的数据使用条款，且绝不出现在训练导出中，由一个导出 fixture 证明。

## Rollout

1. **零号班次（Proving Ground，NDA）。** 已落地：`environment/run` stamp 上的 `district`，连同导出器的 `withheldDistricts` 与按请求的 `districts`；fleet 按路由的熔断器（`FLEET_ROUTE_BREAKER_OPEN`）；其计划级 `tokenCeiling` 与整次运行的 `spend`（`FLEET_TOKEN_CEILING_REACHED`）；其 `workspaceRetention`；组合门禁；预算策略携带价格表摘要的 `usage/priced` 事件；证书上的 executor（读取屏障切片 4）；scorekeeper 把 `usage/priced` 折叠为每次会话的成本与每个已认证会话的成本；以及 stamp 的 `district` 作为观测台据以扣留的 `ScoreboardRow` 键的一部分。仍需要：有人值班运行。
2. **公开证书率。** 需要读取屏障切片 5 与 6（shell 拒绝与篡改裁决）以及篡改列；此后证书率进入归档的 quality 项。
3. **无人值守的班次。** 已在[班次笔记](2026-09-05-village-shifts.md)中设计：班次身份与 `shift/*` 账本、从 stamp 恢复且绝不重跑的 cell、按区的节奏，以及跨班次的 token 花费窗口；其切片落地后，主机级监督进程退为后备。
4. **点名比较与 Commons。** 需要组合清单各切片（stamp 上的摘要、preset 作为实验臂、排行榜上的 `harnessVariantId`）以及带 `parked` 与同胞摘要的归档。
5. **公开的 Workshop 与摘录披露。** 需要 `signoff/recorded`、`dataUse/terms`、强制脱敏与信任档案导出。
6. **任何外联。** 需要 `external-communication` 权限与可拒绝的 monitor。
7. **实时观测台。** 需要作为带缓存会话投影的排行榜；在此之前页面注明其批量刷新间隔。
8. **供给 W3。** 需要 stamp 上的 `policyVersion` 与 `seed`、轨迹折叠中被掩码的终止原因、近重复准入与设备槽位预算。

## Risks

- **夸大标题之下的正确表格。** 初稿的逐行状态是准确的，而它的总标题声称了隐藏检查与受控实验；每一句公开的话都必须能对照状态列核验，否则观测台会以相反的方向重演 Village 的可信度问题。
- **一行缺失。** 一个没有错误行就消失的会话会抬高由其余行算出的每个比率；幸存者偏差是客户评审者第一个要测的东西。
- **harness 与模型的共同演化。** 在针对某路由演化过的 harness 变体上测量该路由，测的是这一对；stamp 上的组合摘要是让排行榜行可归因的东西。
- **比较性声明。** 一家商业实验室无法证实的点名比较是 Village 作为非营利组织从不承担的法律风险敞口。
- **沉没的硬件。** 方案 B 的集群是为训练与数据驻留而配置的，不是为 Village 推理；仅为运行 Village 而购买它是错误的理由。
- **人员成本占主导。** 四名工程师的成本是任一基础设施方案的数倍；设计必须随每个 rollout 步骤降低值班负担，否则无法保持常驻。
- **涌现的制度。** agent 互相编写的技能在没有内容寻址身份与 keep-or-retire 记分板的情况下会漂移成提示膨胀；Village 中 48% 无法复现的自报 bug 是要时刻记住的数字。

8	
9	```
10	packages/<group>/<pkg>/
11	  package.json     # copy from packages/core/tools, adjust name/description/deps
12	  tsconfig.json    # extends ../../../tsconfig.base.json, rootDir src,
13	                   # outDir lib/types, references: ../../../vendor/cosmokit,
14	                   # ../../../vendor/cordis (+ ../../../vendor/schemastery if
15	                   # you use Config, + ../../<group>/<dep> for each dsh dep)
16	  src/index.ts     # service default export or plugin (name/inject/apply/Config)
17	  README.md        # service API, events, extension points, design notes,
18	                   # + gated Model Experience context blocks or short form
19	                   # + the gated "Known Limitations and Deferred Work" section
20	                   # (or a whitelist entry in scripts/verify-package-readme-limitations.ts)
21	```
22	
23	Choose an existing group when one matches the package's role (`core`, `llm`, `bash`, `compact`, `subagent`, `todo`, `session-persistence`, `ui`, `util`, or `support`). A new group is allowed, but it is a pure container: no `package.json`, no source files, and packages still sit exactly one level below it.
24	
25	package.json invariants (enforced by `pnpm run constraints` / `scripts/check-workspace-constraints.ts`): `private: true`, a `version` matching the root `package.json`, `type: module`, `main: "lib/index.js"`, `types: "lib/types/index.d.ts"`, `exports["."].types: "./lib/types/index.d.ts"`, `exports["."].default: "./lib/index.js"`, `@deepseek-ai/cordis` in BOTH peerDependencies and devDependencies (same range). Mirror every dsh peer dependency in devDependencies. `@deepseek-ai/schemastery` goes in `dependencies` (it is a runtime validator), matching agent-loop. The `files` list contains exactly `lib/index.js`, `lib/invariant.js`, `lib/types/**/*.d.ts`, and package-specific runtime artifacts recognized by the gate; a package whose runtime export points into the emitted tree also includes `lib/types/**/*.js`. Do not publish `src`, declaration maps, JS maps, or stale root declaration files. CLI app packages with a package `bin` include `lib/bin.js` immediately after `lib/index.js` in `files`.
26	
27	In-package relative imports use explicit `.ts` specifiers in source (for example, `export * from './types.ts'`). The compiler rewrites those to `.js` in emitted JS and leaves explicit `.ts` specifiers in declarations, which standard NodeNext/Node16 TypeScript consumers resolve to the sibling `.d.ts` files.

30	
31	| File | Change |
32	|---|---|
33	| `tsconfig.base.json` | no edit for an existing group; for a new group, add a `./packages/<group>/*/src` candidate to the `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` wildcard |
34	| `tsconfig.host.json` (Host package) or `tsconfig.client.json` (Client package) | add `{ "path": "./packages/<group>/<pkg>" }` to `references` — an ordinary package belongs to exactly one aggregate, never both. `api/remotes` uses a repository-specific split because the Host generates a contract that the Client consumes in a later phase; new packages must not copy it ([layout](../development.md#typescript-project-layout)) |

41	## 3. Decide the package topology
42	
43	For a swappable capability, separate Service Definition / Service Provider / Consumer roles into packages when they evolve independently (see docs/architecture.md § "Capability seams" — the shell trio is the template). A single-purpose plugin stays one package.
44	
45	### Name the role that exists
46	
47	Name the stable current responsibility. Do not name the first implementation, a possible future expansion, or the Cordis base class. An interface package names the capability. An implementation package adds the mechanism, protocol, environment, or vendor that distinguishes it. Use `local` only when same-host execution is part of the contract.
48	
49	Use a singular `ctx` key for one engine, runtime, policy, controller, resolver, store, or current configuration. Use a plural key for a registry or a service that owns multiple named members. The class role and key number must agree. Do not reuse one Cordis `Context` key for incompatible host and client declarations. TypeScript declaration merging sees both faces even when they use separate runtime contexts. Add the role suffix when the natural plural already belongs to another face.
50	
51	| Word | Use it when | Do not use it when |
52	|---|---|---|
53	| `Controller` | It accepts commands or user intent and changes one existing domain or presentation state. | It executes arbitrary work, owns a provider fleet, or only converts values for display. |
54	| `Store` | It owns one data set and mainly offers CRUD, snapshot, or subscription operations for that data. | It validates a state machine, arbitrates authority, dispatches work, or owns provider precedence. A map does not make a class a store. |
55	| `Directory` | It exposes entries and metadata for discovery or selection. | Producers register arbitrary implementations into it, or callers execute work through it. |
56	| `Presenter` | It is a pure conversion from domain values or tool arguments to render intent. | It performs I/O, subscribes, mutates state, or owns lifecycle. |
57	| `Registry` | It owns a dynamic set of named registrations, including lookup, duplicate or precedence rules, lifetime, and disposal. | Its main contract is dispatch, execution, cancellation, policy, or orchestration. |
58	| `Runtime` | It runs live work and owns dispatch, cancellation, provider coordination, or operation lifecycle across calls. | It only stores records, returns a catalog, resolves one value, or holds configuration. |
59	| `Resolver` | It computes or locates one answer from supplied inputs without owning that answer's lifecycle. | It owns a mutable collection or long-running execution. |
60	| `Binder` | It attaches one declared interface to a caller context or lifecycle and returns the bound value. | It owns the value as a collection, controls its domain state, or only converts data. |
61	| `Engine` | It implements a domain algorithm or stateful execution model. | It only selects a provider or forwards across a protocol boundary. |
62	| `Policy` | It decides what is allowed, selected, limited, or observed. | It performs the mechanism that the decision permits. |
63	| `Executor` | It runs one explicit request or resolved specification in one capability. | It owns a broad application lifecycle or provider catalog. |
64	| `Gateway` | It adapts a process, network, RPC, or API boundary. | It only registers same-process services or stores metadata. |
65	| `Provider` | It supplies one implementation of a capability definition. Add a mechanism or vendor qualifier when several can exist. | It is the capability definition, provider registry, or consumer runtime. |
66	| `Backend` | It implements replaceable lower-level persistence, transport, or execution behind a defined interface. | It is a user-facing service or one returned live-resource reference. |
67	| `Handle` | It refers to one live resource and controls or observes that resource. | It creates and manages the complete resource pool. |
68	| `Config` | It owns one resolved configuration value or one tightly bounded record and its update contract. | It stores a general collection, executes work, or exposes unrelated settings. |
69	| `Service` | It owns a cohesive domain service that no sharper role above states honestly. | The name exists only because the class extends Cordis `Service`. |
70	
71	Use `SDK` only for the JSON-RPC client/server protocol used by the supported Python and TypeScript SDKs. DeepSeek Harness itself is an agent harness, not an SDK project. Use the canonical product spelling `Typert`, never `TypeRT` or `typeRT`.
72	
73	## 4. Write the package README
74	
75	Keep package-specific service API, config, events, extension points, and design notes first. The limitations section records durable consumer gaps and non-obvious maintainer constraints owned by this package; ordinary cleanup stays in its source TODO or Agent Note. An indirect Model Experience sentence may name the consumer that surfaces this package's contribution, but it does not restate that consumer's implementation. End a package README with this canonical sequence:
76	
77	````markdown
78	## Model Experience
79	
80	### Request context and condition
81	
82	#### What the model sees
83	
84	The exact data-dependent fields, an anchored generated-catalog link, or an introduction to the verbatim literal below.
85	
86	##### Verbatim text for this field, when needed
87	
88	```markdown
89	Stable system-prompt prose of any length, or another long non-generated literal, copied exactly from source.
90	```
91	
92	#### Token effect
93	
94	Fixed, conditional, retained, replaced, capped, or zero-direct token effect.
95	
96	#### KV Cache effect
97	
98	Append-only, prefix-stable, replacing, or independent behavior, including the exact conditions that may invalidate reuse.
99	
100	## Known Limitations and Deferred Work
101	
102	- **Consumer-visible gap** — exact missing operation or case, its consequence, and any maintainer constraint.
103	````
104	
105	Fill Model Experience from the implementation. Use one H3 per direct, conditional, capped, lifetime, or auxiliary model-context entry, with the three ordered H4 fields shown above and one prose paragraph under each. Quote stable text owned by the package: system-prompt prose goes in a titled H5 plus `markdown` fence under the field that introduces it—normally `What the model sees`—other short literals stay inline with named placeholders, and other long literals use the same nested form. Summarize only data-dependent or provider-owned text. A tool-schema entry links its anchored section in the generated [tool catalog](../tool-catalog.md) and states only deltas absent there. Keep prompt and schema entries separate when scoping can hide one without the other. In `KV Cache effect`, distinguish append-only growth, a stable repeated prefix, replacement of earlier request tokens, and an independent model request, then name the package-owned changes that can invalidate reuse. “Does not invalidate” means the package preserves an already-reusable prefix; provider cache availability and eviction remain outside the package contract. The [prose standard](../../.agents/skills/dsh-prose-standard/SKILL.md) governs completeness and ownership; the verifier enforces the required section structure.
106	
107	A package with no context effect or one consumer-owned path uses the audited `None, as ` or `Indirectly, through ` sentence in [`SENTENCE_MODEL_EXPERIENCE`](../../scripts/verify-package-readme-model-experience.ts), followed by a `KV Cache effect` H4 and one non-empty paragraph; a model-agnostic generic package may instead join `NO_MODEL_EXPERIENCE_SECTION`. Do not expand either case into a description of another package's work. The limitations [allowlist](../../scripts/verify-package-readme-limitations.ts) is independent. The [Model Experience Agent Note](../../.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-07-12-package-model-experience-contract.md) records the rationale.
108	
109	## 5. Verify
110	
111	```sh
112	pnpm install        # registers the workspace
113	pnpm run doc-sync
114	pnpm run constraints && pnpm run typecheck && pnpm run lint
115	pnpm run build && pnpm run hygiene
116	```
117	
118	Follow the [repository testing policy](../testing.md) for the behavior-specific checks and coverage required by the new package.

- **Initiator-owned private chains derive, then capture.** Under `ctx.agents.withInitiator()`, recover the Agent at each orchestration entry, derive `agent.session`, and let operation-local helpers close over it. Keep `Agent` and `Session` explicit at lifecycle, session-log, service, authority, worker/process, persistence, and wire interfaces; do not widen a leaf helper from `Session` to `Context` merely to hide a parameter ([rationale](../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-15-agent-initiator-scope.md)).
- **Represent one asynchronous operation with one lifecycle controller or transaction.** Separate readiness, cancellation, disposal, reservation, or sentinel state requires an independent owner or settlement point; otherwise fold it while preserving rollback, callback containment, and quiescence.
- **Design Service Definitions for all current Consumers.** Keep tool-schema, Loader, UI, transport, and provider-specific behavior in the Consumer or provider; do not let one Consumer dictate the service contract ([capability-seam rationale](../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-06-13-capability-seams.md)). Inverse smell: a public service method with one internal caller — pass a private capability closure instead (`RunCodeBridgeOptions`).
- **Require a current owner and need.** Tie each abstraction, state machine, option, defensive copy, and compatibility path to a current contract or production consumer, and keep behavior in its owning plugin or service.
- **Require evidence for public choices.** Configurability does not justify an unsupported default, public operation set, format, or imported external concept. Use current-consumer evidence or relevant prior art; otherwise require an explicit value or defer the choice.
- **Write model-facing contracts from the model's perspective.** Prompts, tool schemas, results, and diagnostics contain only task-relevant concepts, not UI, transport, or implementation vocabulary. Pin stable model-visible text verbatim and dynamic behavior through snapshots or end-to-end coverage.
- **Enforce a decision in the operation that makes it.** Schema omission, prompt filtering, facades, wrappers, and listener order are not enforcement when direct or alternate callers can bypass them; test denial through the executor.
- **Publish state only at its commit point.** Emit each notification and update derived state only after the operation succeeds; derive caches, prompts, UI echoes, replay, and query views from one authoritative source.
- **Apply bounds to the complete result.** Enforce byte, token, item, and time limits where the complete emitted or retained value, including wrappers and metadata, is known; test tiny and exact limits, oversized single chunks, and multibyte byte limits.
- **Registry contributions prove disposal** through the HMR-safety test required by [testing policy](../docs/testing.md): dispose the fiber and observe removal.
- **Every package owns `./invariant`.** Register the manifest name; check an event/data relation or give empty installers package-specific `No runtime invariant:` reasons. Generated companions, unexplained empties, and ignored reporters fail [`verify-package-invariants`](../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-19-package-invariant-runtime-contracts.md).

[Naming rules](../docs/cookbook/adding-a-package.md#name-the-role-that-exists):

- **Package tsconfig:** extends `tsconfig.base.json` (Client: `tsconfig.base.client.json`), uses `rootDir: src`, `outDir: lib/types`, and references each workspace dependency plus `runtime-diagnostics/invariants`; registers in exactly one aggregate. Only `api/remotes` splits for generated contracts; ordinary two-entry Client plugins do not ([layout](../docs/development.md#typescript-project-layout)).
- `src/types.ts` contains only types — no runtime code.
- Tests live at package level under `tests/`, not `src/__tests__/`.
- A package's README and JSDoc are part of the change: altered behavior (config keys, defaults, error codes, wire fields) updates them in the same commit. `doc-sync` gates what it can; apply [dsh-prose-standard](../.agents/skills/dsh-prose-standard/SKILL.md) for complete, concise prose and verify accuracy against code.
- Package READMEs document model, token, and KV-cache effects using the [canonical Model Experience format](../docs/cookbook/adding-a-package.md#4-write-the-package-readme).
- Package READMEs put durable consumer gaps and non-obvious maintainer constraints under `## Known Limitations and Deferred Work`; ordinary cleanup stays in its TODO or Agent Note. Packages with none use a justified [allowlist entry](../scripts/verify-package-readme-limitations.ts) ([rationale](../.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-07-10-readme-known-limitations-gate.md)).

</system-reminder>

14	  interface SessionEventMap {

16	     * Opening record of one shift: the identity the slot froze, the digest its
17	     * plan hashes to, the frozen plan verbatim, and the slot time the cadence
18	     * computed. Appended once, before the shift's first cell starts, and the
19	     * only event that tells a later process a shift exists to resume.
20	     */
21	    'shift/start': ShiftStart
22	    /**
23	     * One cell of the shift settled: the cell's coordinates, the session the
24	     * runner created for it when one exists, and its outcome. Appended once
25	     * per cell, after the cell's own session is durable — including for an
26	     * orphan a later process found stamped but unrecorded, which it records as
27	     * `interrupted` and never runs again.
28	     */
29	    'shift/cell': ShiftCellRecord
30	    /**

32	     * cells this process runs. Appended after the orphans of the interrupted
33	     * process are recorded and before the pending cells start.

44	     * cells spent, and the cell counts per outcome. Its presence is what marks

54	 * resolved to against the registry at freeze time, so the digest and the cell

163	}

176	  maxTokens: number
177	}

170	  constructor(ctx: Context, config: Config) {
171	    super(ctx, 'shifts')
172	    this.config = config
173	    if (!isAbsolute(config.workspaceRoot) || !isDirectory(config.workspaceRoot)) {
174	      throw new ShiftError(`workspaceRoot "${config.workspaceRoot}" is not an existing absolute directory`, 'SHIFT_INVALID_CONFIG')
175	    }
176	    if (config.districts.length === 0) throw new ShiftError('the driver is composed with no district', 'SHIFT_INVALID_CONFIG')
177	    const named = new Set<string>()
178	    for (const district of config.districts) {
179	      if (named.has(district.district)) {
180	        throw new ShiftError(`district "${district.district}" is configured twice`, 'SHIFT_INVALID_CONFIG')
181	      }
182	      named.add(district.district)
183	      if (district.plan.models.length === 0) {
184	        throw new ShiftError(`district "${district.district}" names no model route`, 'SHIFT_INVALID_CONFIG')

186	    }

194	   * first, so the plugin's own start and a driver awaiting the first slot
195	   * observe the same run.

197	   *   district is either running its due slot or armed for its next one.

201	    await this.opening

204	  /**
205	   * Stop the loop: disarm every cadence timer, cancel the fleet run in flight
206	   * through its signal, and wait for the slots that are settling. The
207	   * interrupted cells end as the runner ends them and their sessions become
208	   * the orphans the next process records.
209	   * @returns a promise settling once no slot is in flight.

211	  async stop(): Promise<void> {
212	    this.stopping = true
213	    this.controller?.abort(new Error('the shift driver is stopping'))
214	    for (const disarm of this.timers.values()) await disarm()

216	    await Promise.allSettled([...this.running.values()])

236	      if (ledger.end === undefined) await this.resume(ledger, scan.stamped)

244	  /** Arm the district's cadence, then run the slot it already owes. */
245	  private async openDistrict(district: ShiftDistrictConfig, previous: number | undefined): Promise<void> {
246	    const at = nextSlotAt(previous, district.cadence.intervalMs, Date.now(), this.config.startImmediately)
247	    if (at > Date.now()) {
248	      this.arm(district, at)
249	      return
250	    }
251	    this.arm(district, nextSlotAt(at, district.cadence.intervalMs, Date.now(), false))
252	    await this.slot(district, at)

255	  /**
256	   * Replace one district's cadence timer with one firing at `at`. Each firing
257	   * arms the next slot before it runs this one, so slots keep arriving on the
258	   * cadence and a slot that lands on a still-running shift is refused rather
259	   * than delayed into it.
260	   */
261	  private arm(district: ShiftDistrictConfig, at: number): void {
262	    void this.timers.get(district.district)?.()
263	    const disarm = this.ctx.effect(() => {
264	      const timer = setTimeout(() => {
265	        this.arm(district, nextSlotAt(at, district.cadence.intervalMs, Date.now(), false))
266	        // A slot that cannot be frozen must not take the loop down with it: the
267	        // next slot is already armed and the failure is the operator's signal.
268	        void this.slot(district, at).catch((error: unknown) => {
269	          this.ctx.logger.error(`district "${district.district}" slot ${at} failed: ${String(error)}`)
270	        })
271	      }, Math.max(0, at - Date.now()))
272	      return () => {
273	        clearTimeout(timer)
274	      }
275	    }, `shifts.cadence(${district.district})`)
276	    this.timers.set(district.district, disarm)
277	  }

279	  /** Freeze one slot and either refuse it or run it, keeping one shift per district in flight. */
280	  private async slot(district: ShiftDistrictConfig, scheduledAt: number): Promise<void> {
281	    const plan = this.freeze(district)
282	    const digest = shiftDigest(plan)
283	    const id = shiftId(digest, scheduledAt)
284	    if (this.running.has(plan.district)) {
285	      await this.skip(id, { digest, scheduledAt, reason: 'overlap' })
286	      return
287	    }
288	    const inFlight = this.runSlot(district, plan, digest, id, scheduledAt)
289	      .finally(() => {
290	        this.running.delete(plan.district)
291	      })
292	    this.running.set(plan.district, inFlight)
293	    await inFlight
294	  }

298	    district: ShiftDistrictConfig,
299	    plan: ShiftPlan,

331	  private async resume(ledger: ShiftLedger, stamped: readonly StampedCell[]): Promise<void> {
332	    const { plan, shiftId: id } = ledger.start
333	    const cells = shiftCells(plan)
334	    const split = splitPending(cells, ledger, stamped)
335	    const preparation = await this.ctx.sessionPersistence.prepare(ledger.sessionId)
336	    const { session } = preparation

339	        for (const orphan of split.orphans) {
340	          session.append('shift/cell', {
341	            shiftId: id,
342	            cell: orphan.cell,
343	            sessionId: orphan.sessionId,
344	            outcome: { kind: 'interrupted' },
345	          })

356	  /**
357	   * Run the pending cells of one shift through the fleet, writing one
358	   * `shift/cell` per announced cell, and close the ledger.
359	   */
360	  private async drive(
361	    session: Session,
362	    id: string,
363	    plan: ShiftPlan,
364	    pending: readonly FleetCell[],
365	    spent: number,
366	  ): Promise<void> {
367	    if (pending.length === 0) {
368	      await this.close(session, id, 'completed', 0)
369	      return
370	    }
371	    const remaining = plan.tokenCeiling === undefined ? undefined : plan.tokenCeiling - spent
372	    if (remaining !== undefined && remaining < 1) {
373	      await this.close(session, id, 'ceiling', 0)
374	      return
375	    }
376	    const controller = new AbortController()
377	    this.controller = controller
378	    let ceilingReached = false
379	    // The fleet announces a cell after its session is durable and its
380	    // workspace reaped, so the ledger entry only ever follows the fact.
381	    const unobserve = this.ctx.on('fleet/cell', (payload) => {
382	      if (payload.group !== id) return
383	      if (payload.outcome.kind === 'error' && payload.outcome.code === 'FLEET_TOKEN_CEILING_REACHED') ceilingReached = true
384	      session.append('shift/cell', {
385	        shiftId: id,
386	        cell: payload.cell,
387	        ...payload.outcome.kind === 'reported' ? { sessionId: payload.outcome.sessionId } : {},
388	        outcome: payload.outcome.kind === 'reported'
389	          ? { kind: 'reported', certified: payload.outcome.certified }
390	          : { kind: 'error', ...payload.outcome.code === undefined ? {} : { code: payload.outcome.code }, message: payload.outcome.message },
391	      })
392	    })
393	    let report: FleetRunReport
394	    try {
395	      report = await this.ctx.fleet.run({
396	        environments: { ids: plan.environments },
397	        models: plan.models,
398	        repetitions: plan.repetitions,
399	        cells: pending,
400	        workspaceRoot: this.config.workspaceRoot,
401	        group: id,
402	        district: plan.district,
403	        ...remaining === undefined ? {} : { tokenCeiling: remaining },
404	        signal: controller.signal,
405	      })
406	    } finally {
407	      unobserve()
408	      this.controller = undefined
409	    }
410	    const outcome = endOutcome(controller.signal.aborted, ceilingReached)
411	    await this.close(session, id, outcome, report.spend.inputTokens + report.spend.outputTokens)
412	  }

414	  /** Append the closing record over every cell the session holds and flush it. */
415	  private async close(session: Session, id: string, outcome: ShiftEndOutcome, spend: number): Promise<void> {
416	    const records = session.events.flatMap(event => (event.type === 'shift/cell' ? [event.data] : []))
417	    session.append('shift/end', { shiftId: id, outcome, spend, cells: countCells(records) })

421	  /**
422	   * Publish one slot session for the length of the slot, flush it, and detach.
423	   * The entry is owned by this fiber, so a disposal that races a slot removes
424	   * it after {@link ShiftService.stop} has let the slot settle.
425	   */
426	  private async publish(session: Session, body: () => Promise<void> | void): Promise<void> {
427	    const detach = this.ctx.effect(function* (this: ShiftService) {
428	      yield this.ctx.sessions.enter(session)
429	      this.ctx.sessions.announce(session)
430	    }.bind(this), `shifts.slot(${session.id})`)
431	    try {
432	      await body()
433	    } finally {
434	      await this.ctx.sessions.flush(session)
435	      await detach()
436	    }
437	  }

439	  /** Read every persisted session once: the shift ledgers and the grouped run stamps. */
440	  private async scan(): Promise<ShiftScan> {
441	    const ledgers: ShiftLedger[] = []
442	    const stamped: StampedCell[] = []
443	    for (const header of await this.ctx.sessionPersistence.list()) {

468	  /** The environment ids one selection names, in registry order for a filter. */
469	  private select(district: string, selection: FleetEnvironmentSelection): EnvironmentId[] {
470	    // The fleet declares the registry injection this driver reads through; a
471	    // composition without it cannot run a cell at all.
472	    const registry = this.ctx.get('environments')
473	    if (registry === undefined) {
474	      throw new ShiftError(`district "${district}" cannot freeze a plan without the environment registry`, 'SHIFT_INVALID_PLAN')

479	          throw new ShiftError(`environment "${id}" of district "${district}" is not registered`, 'SHIFT_INVALID_PLAN')

481	        return id
482	      })
483	    }
484	    return registry.list(selection.filter).map(definition => definition.id)

2	 * Session budget guard. Configured token, wall-clock, and cost caps are
3	 * measured against the durable session log before every proposed step; the
4	 * first cap the log exceeds is recorded as a `budget/breach` event, blocks any
5	 * active goal, and rejects the step so no further model request is made. Every
6	 * step served by a priced route also gets a durable `usage/priced` record, so
7	 * session cost replays from the log at the rates that priced it.

9	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-budget-policy
10	 */

49	/**
50	 * Per-session ceilings. Every cap is optional and uncapped when omitted, so an
51	 * empty configuration is a valid policy that never stops a step. A cap is
52	 * exceeded only when measured spend is strictly greater than its value, which
53	 * makes `0` an immediate stop and keeps an exactly-on-budget session running.
54	 */
55	export interface Config {
56	  /** Billed input tokens (uncached input plus cache reads and writes) allowed in one session. */
57	  maxInputTokens?: number
58	  /** Output tokens allowed in one session. */
59	  maxOutputTokens?: number
60	  /** Input plus output tokens allowed in one session. */
61	  maxTotalTokens?: number

65	  maxCostEur?: number

83	/** The caps a validated configuration actually enforces, paired with their values. */
84	interface ResolvedConfig {
85	  readonly caps: readonly (readonly [BudgetCapId, number])[]
86	  readonly pricing: Readonly<Record<string, BudgetRoutePricing>>
87	  /** Whether {@link pricing} names any route; an empty table never reads the log. */
88	  readonly prices: boolean
89	  /** {@link pricingTableDigest} of {@link pricing}, computed once at load. */
90	  readonly pricingDigest: string

93	/** Reject a cap that cannot express a ceiling before any session depends on it. */
94	function requireFiniteCap(cap: BudgetCapId, value: number): void {
95	  if (!Number.isFinite(value) || value < 0) {
96	    throw new TypeError(`budget-policy: ${cap} must be a finite non-negative number, got ${String(value)}`)
97	  }
98	}
99	
100	/** Reject a rate that cannot price a route before any session depends on it. */
101	function requireFiniteRate(route: string, field: keyof BudgetRoutePricing, value: number): void {
102	  if (!Number.isFinite(value) || value < 0) {
103	    throw new TypeError(`budget-policy: pricing["${route}"].${field} must be a finite non-negative number, got ${String(value)}`)
104	  }
105	}

107	/**
108	 * Validate one deployment configuration and materialize the enforced caps.
109	 * Every rejection happens at plugin load, before a session can depend on a cap
110	 * the policy could not enforce.
111	 */
112	function resolveBudgetConfig(config: Config): ResolvedConfig {
113	  // The schema defaulted the table — the cast records that runtime fact.
114	  const pricing = config.pricing as Readonly<Record<string, BudgetRoutePricing>>
115	  for (const [route, rates] of Object.entries(pricing)) {
116	    requireFiniteRate(route, 'inputEurPerMillionTokens', rates.inputEurPerMillionTokens)
117	    requireFiniteRate(route, 'outputEurPerMillionTokens', rates.outputEurPerMillionTokens)
118	  }
119	  const prices = Object.keys(pricing).length > 0
120	  if (config.maxCostEur !== undefined && !prices) {
121	    throw new TypeError('budget-policy: maxCostEur needs a non-empty pricing table; an unpriced route has no cost cap')
122	  }
123	  const caps: (readonly [BudgetCapId, number])[] = []
124	  for (const cap of BUDGET_CAP_ORDER) {
125	    const value = config[cap]
126	    if (value === undefined) continue
127	    requireFiniteCap(cap, value)
128	    caps.push([cap, value])
129	  }
130	  return { caps, pricing, prices, pricingDigest: pricingTableDigest(pricing) }
131	}

133	/**
134	 * Build the durable price of one accounted message at the configured rates.
135	 * @param event - a message {@link unpricedUsage} selected, so its route is priced.
136	 * @param resolved - the pricing table and its digest this deployment enforces.
137	 * @returns the record to append for that step.
138	 */
139	function priceMessage(event: AccountedMessage, resolved: ResolvedConfig): UsagePriced {
140	  const { provider, model } = event.data.message.source
141	  // oxlint-disable-next-line typescript/no-non-null-assertion -- unpricedUsage yields only routes the table names
142	  const rates = resolved.pricing[routeKey(provider, model)]!
143	  const inputTokens = billedInputTokens(event.data.usage)
144	  const outputTokens = event.data.usage.outputTokens
145	  return {
146	    turn: event.data.turn,
147	    step: event.data.step,
148	    provider,
149	    model,
150	    inputTokens,
151	    outputTokens,
152	    inputEurPerMillionTokens: rates.inputEurPerMillionTokens,
153	    outputEurPerMillionTokens: rates.outputEurPerMillionTokens,
154	    costEur: costEurFor(inputTokens, outputTokens, rates),
155	    pricingDigest: resolved.pricingDigest,
156	  }
157	}

160	 * Record the price of every priced-route step the log does not price yet. The
161	 * selection is log-derived, so a resumed session prices what its predecessor
162	 * left unpriced and a second call over the same log appends nothing.
163	 * @param agent - the agent whose session log is priced.
164	 * @param resolved - the pricing table and its digest this deployment enforces.
165	 */
166	function priceUnpricedSteps(agent: Agent, resolved: ResolvedConfig): void {
167	  if (!resolved.prices) return
168	  for (const event of unpricedUsage(agent.session.events, resolved.pricing)) {
169	    agent.session.append('usage/priced', priceMessage(event, resolved))
170	  }

173	/**
174	 * Measure the session log against the caps this session actually runs under:
175	 * the configured caps tightened by the session's own `budget/caps` record.
176	 * @param agent - the agent whose session log carries the spend and its caps.
177	 * @param resolved - the caps and pricing this deployment enforces.
178	 * @returns the first breach in {@link BUDGET_CAP_ORDER}, or `undefined` while every cap holds.
179	 */
180	function detectBreach(agent: Agent, resolved: ResolvedConfig): BudgetBreach | undefined {
181	  const caps = tightenedCaps(resolved.caps, foldSessionCaps(agent.session.events))
182	  if (caps.length === 0) return undefined
183	  const spend = foldBudgetSpend(agent.session.events, resolved.pricing)
184	  for (const [cap, limit] of caps) {
185	    const measured = measuredFor(spend, cap)
186	    if (measured > limit) return { cap, measured, limit }
187	  }
188	  return undefined
189	}
190	
191	/**
192	 * Block the session's goal so no goal-round driver continues it. The goal
193	 * domain is optional: a composition without `ctx.goals`, without a current
194	 * goal, or whose goal already left the `active` phase still gets the durable
195	 * breach record and the stopped turn.
196	 */
197	function blockGoal(ctx: Context, agent: Agent, breach: BudgetBreach): void {
198	  const goals = ctx.get('goals')
199	  if (goals === undefined) return
200	  const goal = goals.get(agent)
201	  if (goal === undefined || goal.phase !== 'active') return
202	  goals.block(agent, { id: goal.id, revision: goal.revision }, {
203	    code: BUDGET_EXHAUSTED,
204	    message: `Session budget ${breach.cap} exceeded: ${breach.measured} of ${breach.limit}.`,
205	  })
206	}
207	
208	/**
209	 * Register the pre-step budget check and the pricing records for the lifetime
210	 * of `ctx`.
211	 * @param ctx - plugin context; both listeners are disposed with it.
212	 * @param config - the per-session caps and pricing to enforce.
213	 * @throws {TypeError} when the configuration cannot express the caps it declares.
214	 */
215	export function apply(ctx: Context, config: Config): void {
216	  const resolved = resolveBudgetConfig(config)
217	
218	  // Prepended so the budget decision precedes every listener that would build
219	  // request context or reserve continuation work for a step that cannot run.
220	  ctx.on('agent/pre-step', async ({ agent }, next): Promise<PreStepDecision> => {
221	    // Priced before the caps are read, so the last message before a breach is
222	    // priced by the same step that records the breach.
223	    priceUnpricedSteps(agent, resolved)
224	    const breach = detectBreach(agent, resolved)
225	    if (breach === undefined) return next()
226	    agent.session.append('budget/breach', breach)
227	    blockGoal(ctx, agent, breach)
228	    return { kind: 'reject' }
229	  }, { prepend: true })
230	
231	  // A turn that closes normally opens no further step, so its final message is
232	  // priced at the stop boundary instead.
233	  ctx.on('agent/turn-stopping', ({ agent }) => {
234	    priceUnpricedSteps(agent, resolved)
235	  })
236	}
237

1	/**
2	 * Package-owned invariants over the two durable records this package writes.
3	 *
4	 * Every `budget/breach` states a measurement that the events preceding it
5	 * reproduce. Token and wall-clock caps are folded from the log alone, so the
6	 * companion recomputes them independently of the policy that wrote the record;
7	 * `maxCostEur` depends on the deployment pricing table, which is not in the
8	 * log, so a cost breach is checked only for the exceeded-its-limit relation
9	 * every breach must satisfy.
10	 *
11	 * Every `usage/priced` cites one earlier `assistant/message` of the same step
12	 * whose accounting and route it reproduces, prices its own recorded tokens at
13	 * its own recorded rates, and is the first record of that step — the rates come
14	 * from the record itself, so cost is recomputable from the log alone.
15	 *
16	 * Every `budget/caps` only ever tightens the caps the same log already carries.
17	 * The deployment's configured caps are not in the log, so widening one of those
18	 * is invisible here and is refused by the enforcing fold instead; what this
19	 * companion owns is the relation between successive records of one session,
20	 * where a later record that raises an earlier cap would hand the session budget
21	 * its own log already denied it.
22	 *
23	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-budget-policy/invariant
24	 */
25	
26	import type { Context } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'
27	import { sessionEventValidator } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-invariants'
28	import type { InvariantFailure, InvariantInstaller } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-invariants'
29	import type { SessionEvent } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session'
30	import { BUDGET_CAP_ORDER, foldBudgetSpend, foldSessionCaps, measuredFor } from './fold.ts'
31	import { billedInputTokens, costEurFor, routeKey } from './pricing.ts'
32	import type { BudgetBreach, BudgetCaps, UsagePriced } from './types.ts'
33	
34	const PACKAGE_NAME = '@deepseek-ai/dsh-budget-policy'
35	
36	/** Cordis companion plugin name. */
37	export const name = 'budget-policy-invariant'
38	/** Service required before the companion can reserve package ownership. */
39	export const inject = ['invariants']
40	
41	/** Validate one recorded breach against the durable prefix that precedes it. */
42	function validateBreach(
43	  prior: readonly SessionEvent[],
44	  breach: BudgetBreach,
45	  fail: InvariantFailure,
46	): void {
47	  const { cap, measured, limit } = breach
48	  if (!(measured > limit)) {
49	    fail(`budget/breach records ${cap} measured ${measured} which does not exceed its limit ${limit}`)
50	  }
51	  // Cost is priced from configuration the log does not carry, so only the
52	  // log-derived caps are recomputable here.
53	  if (cap === 'maxCostEur') return
54	  const recomputed = measuredFor(foldBudgetSpend(prior, {}), cap)
55	  if (recomputed !== measured) {
56	    fail(`budget/breach records ${cap} measured ${measured}, but folding the preceding events yields ${recomputed}`)
57	  }
58	}
59	
60	/** Validate one recorded price against the durable prefix that precedes it. */
61	function validatePriced(
62	  prior: readonly SessionEvent[],
63	  priced: UsagePriced,
64	  fail: InvariantFailure,
65	): void {
66	  const step = `turn ${priced.turn} step ${priced.step}`
67	  for (const earlier of prior) {
68	    if (earlier.type !== 'usage/priced') continue
69	    if (earlier.data.turn !== priced.turn || earlier.data.step !== priced.step) continue
70	    fail(`usage/priced prices ${step}, which seq ${earlier.seq} already priced`)
71	  }
72	  const cited = prior.find((event): event is SessionEvent<'assistant/message'> =>
73	    event.type === 'assistant/message' && event.data.turn === priced.turn && event.data.step === priced.step)
74	  if (cited === undefined) return fail(`usage/priced prices ${step}, which no preceding assistant/message reports`)
75	  const usage = cited.data.usage
76	  if (usage === undefined
77	    || billedInputTokens(usage) !== priced.inputTokens
78	    || usage.outputTokens !== priced.outputTokens) {
79	    fail(`usage/priced prices ${priced.inputTokens} input and ${priced.outputTokens} output tokens for ${step}, which its assistant/message does not report`)
80	  }
81	  const { provider, model } = cited.data.message.source
82	  if (provider !== priced.provider || model !== priced.model) {
83	    fail(`usage/priced prices ${step} on route ${routeKey(priced.provider, priced.model)}, which its assistant/message reports as ${routeKey(provider, model)}`)
84	  }
85	  const recomputed = costEurFor(priced.inputTokens, priced.outputTokens, priced)
86	  if (recomputed !== priced.costEur) {
87	    fail(`usage/priced records costEur ${priced.costEur} for ${step}, but its own rates price its own tokens at ${recomputed}`)
88	  }
89	}
90	
91	/** Validate one recorded set of caps against the caps the same log already carries. */
92	function validateCaps(
93	  prior: readonly SessionEvent[],
94	  caps: BudgetCaps,
95	  fail: InvariantFailure,
96	): void {
97	  const standing = foldSessionCaps(prior)
98	  for (const cap of BUDGET_CAP_ORDER) {
99	    const recorded = caps[cap]
100	    const earlier = standing[cap]
101	    if (earlier === undefined) continue
102	    if (recorded === undefined) {
103	      fail(`budget/caps drops ${cap}, which this session's own log caps at ${earlier}`)
104	      continue
105	    }
106	    if (recorded > earlier) {
107	      fail(`budget/caps raises ${cap} to ${recorded}, which this session's own log caps at ${earlier}`)
108	    }
109	  }
110	}
111	
112	/** Validate one candidate event against the durable prefix that precedes it. */
113	function validateEvent(
114	  prior: readonly SessionEvent[],
115	  event: SessionEvent,
116	  fail: InvariantFailure,
117	): void {
118	  if (event.type === 'budget/breach') {
119	    validateBreach(prior, event.data, fail)
120	    return
121	  }
122	  if (event.type === 'budget/caps') {
123	    validateCaps(prior, event.data, fail)
124	    return
125	  }
126	  if (event.type === 'usage/priced') validatePriced(prior, event.data, fail)
127	}
128	
129	/** Check existing sessions and every candidate event before Session publishes it. */
130	const install: InvariantInstaller = sessionEventValidator(validateEvent, ctx => ctx.sessions.list())
131	
132	/**
133	 * Register the budget-record invariant companion.
134	 * @param ctx - Cordis context carrying the invariant service.
135	 * @returns the installed registration's disposer after setup succeeds.
136	 */
137	export const apply = (ctx: Context): Promise<() => void> =>
138	  Promise.resolve(ctx.invariants.register(PACKAGE_NAME, install))

/**
 * Wire-safe approval identifiers and outcome vocabulary, free of
 * cordis/service imports so browser type chains (apiproxy api → client) can
 * consume them without loading this package's Context augmentation.
 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-user-approval/types
 */

import type { Branded } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-brand'

/**
 * Pairs one `approval/asked` audit event with its `approval/decided`.
 * Service-issued (one fresh id per {@link ApprovalService.request} call).
 */
export type ApprovalRequestId = Branded<'ApprovalRequestId'>

/**
 * Brand a string as an {@link ApprovalRequestId}.
 * @param id - the raw id string to brand.
 * @returns the same string carrying the brand.
 */
export function ApprovalRequestId(id: string): ApprovalRequestId {
  return id as ApprovalRequestId
}

/**
 * Closed approval outcomes: a one-shot grant, explicit rejection, withdrawn
 * request, or unavailable answerer. Callers fail closed on `unavailable`.
 */
export type ApprovalOutcome = 'allowed-once' | 'rejected' | 'cancelled' | 'unavailable'

1	/**
2	 * Service Definition for the approval capability seam, covering requests, cancellation, audit, and per-session policy. Missing
3	 * answerers fail closed; grants apply only to the requested action.
4	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-user-approval
5	 */
6	
7	import { randomUUID } from 'node:crypto'
8	import { Context, Service } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'
9	import z from '@deepseek-ai/schemastery'
10	import type { Agent } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent'
11	import { createUserMessage, type CallId } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm'
12	import { scopeTarget } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-scope'
13	import type { Scoped } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-scope'
14	import type { Session, SessionEvent } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session'
15	import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-system-prompt'
16	
17	declare module '@deepseek-ai/cordis' {
18	  interface Context {
19	    approval: ApprovalService
20	  }
21	
22	  interface Events {
23	    /**
24	     * Ask composed answerers for one decision. Return an outcome to claim the
25	     * request or call `next()`; failure yields the fail-closed default.
26	     * Scope-filtered dispatch (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-scope`): agent-scoped listeners receive only that agent.
27	     * @param req - the pending decision (agent, tool identity, reason, signal).
28	     * @mode waterfall
29	     */
30	    'approval/request'(this: Scoped<ApprovalService>, req: ApprovalRequest, next: () => Promise<ApprovalOutcome>): Promise<ApprovalOutcome>
31	  }
32	}
33	
34	declare module '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session/types' {
35	  interface SessionEventMap {
36	    /**
37	     * An approval question was put to the answerer chain — log-only audit
38	     * (like `hook/*`; NOT a surface event, carries no `surfaceOp`). `id` pairs
39	     * it with the `approval/decided` that always follows; `toolName` is the
40	     * tool the question is about, `callId` the exact tool call when the asker
41	     * had one, `reason` the asker's human-readable explanation (e.g. a hook's
42	     * permission-decision reason).
43	     */
44	    'approval/asked': {
45	      id: ApprovalRequestId
46	      toolName: string
47	      callId?: CallId
48	      reason?: string
49	    }
50	    /**
51	     * The outcome of a prior `approval/asked` (same `id`) — log-only audit.
52	     * Exactly one per ask, appended when the outcome is known: a decision, a
53	     * cancellation, or the fail-closed `'unavailable'`.
54	     */
55	    'approval/decided': {
56	      id: ApprovalRequestId
57	      outcome: ApprovalOutcome
58	    }
59	    /**
60	     * The session's approval policy was switched — log-only, durable,
61	     * replayable, never in the model transcript (the model learns the policy
62	     * from the runtime-context snapshot and live switch notices). The LAST
63	     * such event is the session's override ({@link effectiveApprovalPolicy}).
64	     * `source: 'delegation'` marks an override seeded into a child; an absent
65	     * source is a runtime switch.
66	     */
67	    'approval/policy': {
68	      policy: ApprovalPolicy
69	      /** Marks an override seeded into a child at delegation. */
70	      source?: 'delegation'
71	    }
72	  }
73	}
74	
75	import { ApprovalRequestId } from './types.ts'
76	import type { ApprovalOutcome } from './types.ts'
77	
78	export { ApprovalRequestId } from './types.ts'
79	export type { ApprovalOutcome } from './types.ts'
80	
81	/** Every {@link ApprovalOutcome}, for runtime normalization of answerer returns. */
82	const OUTCOMES: readonly ApprovalOutcome[] = ['allowed-once', 'rejected', 'cancelled', 'unavailable']
83	
84	/**
85	 * A session's approval policy — what happens to an {@link ApprovalService}
86	 * ask BEFORE any interactive answerer sees it:
87	 *
88	 * - `'ask'` (the default) — delegate to the composed answerers; with none
89	 *   composed the chain falls through to the fail-closed `'unavailable'`.
90	 * - `'never'` — never prompt anyone: every ask resolves `'rejected'`
91	 *   deterministically. The strict headless stance (CI, unattended runs) and
92	 *   the policy whose outcome is knowable without asking.
93	 */
94	export type ApprovalPolicy = 'ask' | 'never'
95	
96	/** Every {@link ApprovalPolicy}, for option advertisement and runtime validation of untrusted policy strings. */
97	export const APPROVAL_POLICIES: readonly ApprovalPolicy[] = ['ask', 'never']
98	
99	/** Model-facing statement for the deterministic `'never'` policy. */
100	const NEVER_SENTENCE = 'Approval prompts are disabled in this session: actions that require approval are rejected automatically — do not request sandbox escalation (do not set `sandbox_permissions`).'
101	/** Model-facing statement for an interactive policy that may still fail closed. */
102	const ASK_SENTENCE = 'Approval policy: ask. Operations that require approval may ask through the configured answerers; without an available answerer, the request fails closed.'
103	
104	/**
105	 * The session's approval-policy override: the last `approval/policy` event in
106	 * the log, or undefined when the session never switched (callers apply the
107	 * plugin's configured default). The pure fold — resume needs no catch-up
108	 * machinery because replaying the log IS the state.
109	 * @param events - session events in log order (other event types are skipped).
110	 * @returns the policy of the last switch event, or undefined without one.
111	 */
112	export function effectiveApprovalPolicy(events: readonly SessionEvent[]): ApprovalPolicy | undefined {
113	  for (let index = events.length - 1; index >= 0; index -= 1) {
114	    const event = events[index] as SessionEvent
115	    if (event.type === 'approval/policy') return event.data.policy
116	  }
117	  return undefined
118	}
119	
120	/**
121	 * Whether the log currently sits inside an open turn (a `turn/start` not yet
122	 * closed by a `turn/end`) — the {@link ApprovalService.request} precondition.
123	 * The audit pair must be turn-enclosed: the turn is the durable log's
124	 * commit/replay boundary, so a bare event appended between turns is
125	 * indistinguishable from a crash tail and silently dropped on reload.
126	 */
127	function hasOpenTurn(events: readonly SessionEvent[]): boolean {
128	  for (let index = events.length - 1; index >= 0; index -= 1) {
129	    const type = (events[index] as SessionEvent).type
130	    if (type === 'turn/start') return true
131	    if (type === 'turn/end') return false
132	  }
133	  return false
134	}
135	
136	/**
137	 * Append the sole durable representation of a session policy override. Invalid
138	 * values throw before the log changes; consumers fold the new value on each read.
139	 * @param session - the session the override belongs to.
140	 * @param policy - the policy in effect until the next switch.
141	 */
142	export function setApprovalPolicy(session: Session, policy: ApprovalPolicy): void {
143	  if (!APPROVAL_POLICIES.includes(policy)) {
144	    throw new TypeError('approval policy must be one of "ask" or "never"')
145	  }
146	  session.append('approval/policy', { policy })
147	}
148	
149	/**
150	 * Readonly same-process permission question. `callId` links to an already
151	 * presented tool call, so arguments are not duplicated here.
152	 */
153	export interface ApprovalRequest {
154	  /**
155	   * The agent on whose behalf the question is asked. Routes the question (a
156	   * UI answerer only answers for agents it owns) and receives the audit
157	   * events on its session log.
158	   */
159	  readonly agent: Agent
160	  /** The tool the question is about (presentation and audit). */
161	  readonly toolName: string
162	  /**
163	   * The exact tool call being decided, when the asker has one — lets a UI
164	   * attach the prompt to the tool call it already streamed.
165	   */
166	  readonly callId?: CallId
167	  /** The asker's human-readable explanation of WHY it is asking. */
168	  readonly reason?: string
169	  /**
170	   * Aborting withdraws the question: the request settles `'cancelled'`
171	   * immediately and a late answer from a still-pending answerer is discarded.
172	   */
173	  readonly signal?: AbortSignal
174	}

176	/** Plugin config. All optional — `static Config` supplies the defaults. */
177	export interface Config {
178	  /**
179	   * The deployment's default {@link ApprovalPolicy} for sessions without an
180	   * `approval/policy` override — `'ask'` delegates to the composed answerers
181	   * (fail-closed with none); `'never'` auto-rejects every ask without
182	   * prompting (the deterministic CI/unattended stance).
183	   */

185	}

187	/**
188	 * Approval service that applies session policy before answerers and logs every
189	 * ask/outcome pair to the requesting session. It exposes deterministic policy
190	 * changes to the model through the runtime-context snapshot and switch notices.
191	 */
192	export class ApprovalService extends Service {
193	  static Config: z<Config> = z.object({
194	    policy: z.union(['ask', 'never'] as const).default('ask'),
195	  })
196	
197	  constructor(ctx: Context, public config: Config) {
198	    super(ctx, 'approval')
199	
200	    const effective = (agent: Agent): ApprovalPolicy => this.effectivePolicy(agent.session)
201	
202	    // The complete current value travels after retained history, so switching
203	    // policy does not rewrite the stable system-prompt cache prefix.
204	    ctx.inject(['systemPrompt'], (scope: Context) => {
205	      scope.systemPrompt.context({
206	        name: 'approval:policy',
207	        order: 115,
208	        text: (context) => {
209	          const agent = context.agent
210	          // A bare assemble() (tests, diagnostics) has no session to state.
211	          if (agent === undefined) return ''
212	          const policy = effective(agent)
213	          return policy === 'never' ? NEVER_SENTENCE : ASK_SENTENCE
214	        },
215	      })
216	    })
217	  }
218	
219	  /**
220	   * Switch one live agent's policy and queue the transition for its next model
221	   * step. Session initialization uses {@link setApprovalPolicy} directly
222	   * because there is no previously visible policy to change.
223	   * @param agent - the live agent whose policy is changing.
224	   * @param policy - the new effective policy.
225	   */
226	  setPolicy(agent: Agent, policy: ApprovalPolicy): void {
227	    const previous = this.effectivePolicy(agent.session)
228	    if (previous === policy) return
229	    setApprovalPolicy(agent.session, policy)
230	    agent.inject(createUserMessage({
231	      content: [{
232	        type: 'text',
233	        text: `The approval policy changed from "${previous}" to "${policy}" (changed by the user).`,
234	      }],
235	      source: { kind: 'plugin', plugin: 'user-approval' },
236	    }))
237	  }
238	
239	  /**
240	   * Ask the composed answerers to decide one readonly same-process request.
241	   * The service borrows the request, agent, session, and live signal directly.
242	   * The request requires an open turn because the audit pair must be enclosed
243	   * by the durable log's commit/replay boundary; an idle ask rejects before
244	   * appending anything. The answerer phase always produces an outcome: an
245	   * aborted signal yields `'cancelled'`, a missing or throwing answerer yields
246	   * `'unavailable'` (fail closed), and a rogue non-vocabulary return value is
247	   * normalized to `'unavailable'`. A failure that prevents either audit append
248	   * from committing still rejects because returning an unlogged decision would
249	   * violate the pair. Session contains post-commit observer failures, so an
250	   * authoritative append cannot reject the request or suppress its matching
251	   * audit event.
252	   * @param req - the pending decision (agent, tool identity, reason, signal).
253	   * @returns the closed outcome; `'allowed-once'` is the only grant.
254	   * @throws when no turn is open or either audit event fails before the session
255	   *   append commit point.
256	   */
257	  async request(req: ApprovalRequest): Promise<ApprovalOutcome> {
258	    const session = req.agent.session
259	    if (!hasOpenTurn(session.events)) {

263	        + 'Ask from inside the turn that needs the decision.',

277	
278	  /**
279	   * The session's effective policy: its own `approval/policy` fold, else the
280	   * configured default (the schema already defaulted an omitted policy to

26	/** Validate one approval event against committed unmatched questions. */
27	function validateApprovalEvent(
28	  trace: ApprovalTrace,
29	  event: SessionEvent,
30	  fail: InvariantFailure,
31	): ApprovalTransition | undefined {
32	  if (event.type === 'approval/asked') {
33	    if (trace.openTurn === null) fail('approval/asked appended outside any open turn')
34	    if (event.data.toolName.length === 0) fail('approval/asked toolName must be non-empty')
35	    if (trace.pending.has(event.data.id)) fail(`approval/asked repeated open id ${JSON.stringify(event.data.id)}`)
36	    return { kind: 'asked', id: event.data.id }
37	  }
38	  if (event.type === 'approval/decided') {
39	    if (trace.openTurn === null) fail('approval/decided appended outside any open turn')
40	    if (!trace.pending.has(event.data.id)) fail(`approval/decided has no matching approval/asked for id ${JSON.stringify(event.data.id)}`)
41	    if (!APPROVAL_OUTCOMES.includes(event.data.outcome)) {
42	      fail(`approval/decided carries unknown outcome ${JSON.stringify(event.data.outcome)}`)
43	    }
44	    return { kind: 'decided', id: event.data.id }
45	  }

# AGENTS.md

DeepSeek Harness is a plugin-based agent harness on vendored Cordis: **everything is a plugin**. Read [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md) before changing `packages/`; follow [docs/AGENTS.md](docs/AGENTS.md) for documentation.

## Pre-release stance: foundation over blast radius

**Remove this section at the first tagged release.** With no external consumers, prefer the correct foundation over compatibility shims: rename or repackage freely and update every reference together. Backends reject old on-disk formats. SQLite uses monotonic `SCHEMA_VERSION`; `dsh-session` keeps `SESSION_FORMAT_VERSION` at `0` with no compatibility promise.

## Repository layout

```

packages/    @deepseek-ai/dsh-<pkg> workspaces at packages/<group>/<pkg>/
  core/        product API spine: session, system-prompt, tools, agent, agent-loop
  api/         Remote BFF assembly and Typert RPC gateway
  typert/      type graph generator, loader, and runtime registry
  llm/         LLM capability: Service Definition/Consumer + DeepSeek providers
  e2b/         E2B POC: sandbox + FS/subprocess adapters
  shell/        bash capability: Service Definition + local/pwsh providers + shell Consumers
  subprocess/  subprocess capability + local process-tree provider
  terminal/         persistent sessions
  fs/          filesystem capability + policy
  lsp/         language-server capability
  skill/       skill provider registry + local impl + catalog/loader tool
  web/         web capability: Service Definition + search/fetch providers + tool Consumer
  compaction/     compaction capability + basic provider
  context/     request-context plugins
  subagent/    subagent capability: Service Definition + providers + delegation Consumers
  bundle/      installable dsh --profile patch-layer bundles
  workflow/    workflow capability + worker-thread provider + tool Consumer
  todo/        todo_write tool
  plan/        plan mode as logged state
  preset/      per-session agent composition from preset cordis.yml files
  guard/       loop-hygiene, tool-timeout, session-budget plugins
